changes.title: AWS Transit Gateway now shares resource context with firewalls for segmentation policies
changes.detail: AWS Transit Gateway now supports context sharing with security services, such as attached firewalls, allowing you to use Amazon Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs), VPC subnets, VPC security groups, and transit gateway attachments in firewall policies alongside IP addresses. Until now, attached firewalls segmented traffic by IP address, which is hard to plan and maintain, or by resource tags, which firewalls periodically synchronize with IP addresses and can miss new workloads in between. With this feature, you can enforce segmentation based on how workloads and attachments are defined in AWS. Trans

changes.title: AWS Security Hub now detects when vulnerable software is running on Amazon EC2 instances
changes.detail: AWS Security Hub now detects when software with a known vulnerability is actively running on your Amazon EC2 instances. Exposure findings now include a new trait, *The EC2 instance is running software with a known vulnerability*. These findings get a higher severity rating than findings for the same vulnerability where the software isn't running. This helps your security team focus on the vulnerabilities that pose the greatest risk, without investing time and resources to investigate if the software is actually in use. changes.title: AWS Security Hub Network Scanning now supports scanning Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) database instances
changes.detail: AWS Security Hub Network Scanning now scans Amazon RDS DB instances to identify those that are reachable from the internet. Network Scanning automatically discovers existing and new RDS DB instances in your accounts and scans each instance that has Public Access configured. For each reachable port associated with a DB instance, Security Hub creates a finding with details about the instance and the reachable port. changes.title: Cloud Monitoring: Change (November 17, 2026)
changes.detail: Ops Agent version 2.72.0 changed the processing of all supported logging pipelines from the Logging Agent service to the Metric Agent service. When you upgrade from an earlier version of the Ops Agent to version 2.72.0 or later, you will see duplicated logs for a period, because each service maintains its own record of the logs it has processed. This is expected. If the duplicated logs are causing problems, then you can temporarily reconfigure the agent to continue using the Logging Agent service. For more information, see Upgraded logging pipelines .
